summary.headline: Senores Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to INR180 crores and EBITDA 87% to INR54 crores (~30% margin); FY27 guidance is 30-40% revenue and 50-60% PAT growth.
summary.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations was INR180 crores, up 36% YoY, led by regulated markets (up 42%) and emerging markets (up 30%). EBITDA was INR54 crores (up 87%, margin ~30%, up 810 bps) and PAT was INR31 crores (up 56%). Sequentially, absolute EBITDA and PAT dipped versus Q4 FY26, which management attributed mainly to about INR14-15 crores of forex gains in Q4 that did not recur. Management reiterated FY27 guidance and a INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue ambition in three to four years, while the company shifted INR100 crores of IPO proceeds from sterile injectables to oral solids capacity.</overview>

segments.name: Regulated markets (US)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 42% YoY in Q1 FY27. ANDA portfolio rose from 30 (June 2025) to about 58 approved (June 2026), with 23 commercialised and 35 planned over the next 18-20 months.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 30% YoY; EBITDA margin was about 14% (mid-teens) against about 20% in Q4 FY26. Management guides 18-20% for the full year and says the business is cash flow positive, with INR18 crores operating cash in Q1.

segments.name: India branded generics
segments.commentary: Revenue was INR8 crores in Q1 FY27. Management shifted focus to profitability, targeting INR50-60 crores for FY27 at 35-40% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Apnar facility (Baroda, USFDA approved)
segments.commentary: Utilisation is about 80-90% of production capacity, though much of it goes to qualification and launch batches. About six products have been commercialised from Apnar, and about 30 million units were produced in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 30-40% and PAT growth of about 50-60%, with similar growth expected thereafter.
Revenue ambition of INR2,500-3,000 crores in three to four years, based on the current pipeline and excluding NDA products; management said variance of 5-10% is possible in any given year.
FY27 capex of about INR100-120 crores across subsidiaries, with a run rate of INR60-75 crores in the following year.
Emerging market EBITDA margin target of 18-20% on a full-year basis.
Branded generics FY27 revenue target of INR50-60 crores, with 30-40% YoY growth expected.
Zoraya (US front-end) and Amerisyn (US government business) expected to become operational around September-October 2026.
Management expects a 70:30 regulated to emerging market revenue mix to hold for at least the next few years.
Chhatral facility PIC/S approval targeted around Q2-Q3 FY27, opening access to markets such as Vietnam, South Africa and Mexico.
capex_capacity: Apnar (Baroda) facility is at about 80-90% production capacity utilisation, though a large part goes to product qualification and launches. Third production line is under work and a fourth is planned.
Capex is being spent on oral solid capacity in the US and India, plus a scaled-down sterile injectable pilot plant. Shareholder approval for the object change is pending.
Sterile injectable project has about INR100 crores of IPO proceeds left, now pushed to the second half of FY27 with a pilot approach.
Of the 18 products mapped for Apnar, about six are commercialised; portfolio rationalisation between US and India sites is planned from next year.
Management said the Chhatral site in Ahmedabad is PIC/S inspected and makes oral solids, injectables and liquids.

qa_highlights.question: Why did emerging market EBITDA margin fall from about 20% in Q4 FY26 to 14% in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is seasonally weaker than H2, and Q1 is still the strongest first quarter in four years. Management reiterated the full-year 18-20% margin target and cited product mix and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did branded generics decline 2%, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus has moved from sales to profitability after the business rose from INR8 crores to INR40 crores in FY26. It targets INR50-60 crores at 35-40% EBITDA margin for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 'other income' restated for June 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said there is no restatement or policy change. Forex gains were moved from above the operating line into other income, so the presentation changed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sequential EBITDA and PAT decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 included about INR14-15 crores of forex gains that were nil in Q1 FY27. Excluding this, margins are in line sequentially.

qa_highlights.question: Why was IPO proceeds use changed from sterile injectables to oral solids?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Apnar acquisition and oral solid pipeline growth needed capacity sooner, so it reallocated proceeds to oral solid lines in the US and India. A small sterile injectable pilot will follow, and shareholder approval is pending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans, and what is Apnar's utilisation and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR100-120 crores across subsidiaries, and the run rate is INR60-75 crores after that. Apnar utilisation is 80-90% but partly used for qualification; revenue was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 PAT growth be similar to FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a FY28 number and pointed to the INR2,500-3,000 crore revenue goal in three to four years. It said the EBITDA margin of about 30% is the minimum to sustain.
